summary.headline: robots.txt grants OpenAI's complete agent set (retrieval and training alike) broad access while blanket-disallowing Anthropic's and Perplexity's complete agent sets from the entire site -- a deliberate, company-level asymmetry, not a training-vs-retrieval distinction — critical severity, Confirm whether granting OpenAI's agents broad access while blocking Anthropic's and Perplexity's equivalents is an intentional, disclosed licensing arrangement; if it is, state it in the file the way the existing legal notice states the general policy, and if it is not intentional, extend the same treatment given to OAI-SearchBot to Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot.

findings.title: robots.txt grants OpenAI's complete agent set (retrieval and training alike) broad access while blanket-disallowing Anthropic's and Perplexity's complete agent sets from the entire site -- a deliberate, company-level asymmetry, not a training-vs-retrieval distinction
findings.evidence: robots.txt opens with an explicit legal notice prohibiting automated collection for 'development or operation of any artificial intelligence, machine learning, or large language model (LLM) technology... or using it for retrieval-augmented generation' -- a clearly deliberate, carefully-worded policy, not an oversight. Yet the file's actual rules treat AI companies asymmetrically rather than applying that stated principle evenly. Verified directly against a real recipe page path using this audit's own robots.txt parser: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User and OAI-SearchBot -- OpenAI's complete retrieval-and-training set -- all resolve 'allowed' (grouped together, disallowed only from /thmb/ thumbnail assets). ClaudeBot, Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot -- Anthropic's complete retrieval-and-training set -- and PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User -- Perplexity's complete set -- all resolve 'disallowed' from the entire site. Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot are specifically retrieval/answer-engine agents (per this skill's own ai-crawler-agents.md): blocking them removes the site from Claude's and Perplexity's live answers today, the exact harm this audit exists to catch, while the equivalent OpenAI agent (OAI-SearchBot) faces no such block. This is not the defensible 'block training, permit retrieval' pattern documented elsewhere in this project's calibration -- it is a per-company split that happens to favor one AI company's live answer-engine presence over two others'.

reproduction.observed: ChatGPT-User/OAI-SearchBot/GPTBot grouped with Disallow: /thmb/ only; Google-Extended/anthropic-ai/CCBot/Claude-SearchBot/cohere-ai/Meta-ExternalAgent/meta-webindexer/PerplexityBot grouped with Disallow: / (narrow presented/integrated exceptions); ClaudeBot/Claude-User/Perplexity-User grouped in a further Disallow: / list with no exceptions at all
reproduction.expected: Either the stated anti-AI-collection policy applied evenly across companies, or a stated rationale for why OpenAI's retrieval agent is treated differently from Anthropic's and Perplexity's equivalent agents

suggested_action.summary: Confirm whether granting OpenAI's agents broad access while blocking Anthropic's and Perplexity's equivalents is an intentional, disclosed licensing arrangement; if it is, state it in the file the way the existing legal notice states the general policy, and if it is not intentional, extend the same treatment given to OAI-SearchBot to Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot.
suggested_action.mechanism: As written, a user asking Claude or Perplexity about a recipe this site actually has can never be shown this site as a source, while the same question asked of ChatGPT can be -- an asymmetry in AI-answer-engine visibility that is invisible to a site owner who only checks 'is my robots.txt blocking AI' as a single yes/no question, since the honest answer here is 'it depends which AI.'
steps: Confirm with legal/business teams whether this reflects an actual OpenAI-specific agreement.
If intentional, add a comment stating the rationale, consistent with the file's existing legal-notice comment.
If unintentional, align Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot's treatment with OAI-SearchBot's.
suggested_action.verification: Every AI company's retrieval-specific agent (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) receives the same robots.txt treatment, or the file states why one is treated differently.

not_assessed.check: Whether the robots.txt asymmetry documented in the crawl-access finding has any practical effect at the infrastructure level for the agents it names as allowed (render-extractability-audit, structured-data-audit, answerability-audit, freshness-corroboration-audit, engagement-audit -- all content-dependent checks)
not_assessed.reason: Every plain-HTTP fetch attempted from this run's network environment -- the homepage, a declared sitemap file, and four separate agent user-agents (GPTBot, Googlebot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) -- was rejected by Cloudflare (a full JS challenge for browser-like requests: HTTP 403 with a 'cf-mitigated: challenge' response header; a terse HTTP 402/460 rejection for bot-pattern user agents), including GPTBot, which robots.txt itself names as allowed. Pausing between requests did not change the outcome, ruling out simple burst-sensitivity. However, allrecipes.com is an extremely high-traffic, mainstream site that plainly continues to serve ordinary visitors and remains indexed by search engines -- a genuine site-wide block on all browser-like traffic is not plausible, and Cloudflare Bot Management is well known to verify a declared crawler's IP/reverse-DNS against the operator's real infrastructure before granting 'verified bot' treatment. This audit's requests, sent with a matching user-agent string but not from that operator's real IP range, cannot be distinguished from a genuine block on the real agent using only the evidence available here. Per this skill's own guardrail against inferring a block from a network failure on the auditing machine, no technical-block finding is published from this observation.
not_assessed.impact: This audit cannot say whether OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot or PerplexityBot's real, IP-verified traffic actually reaches allrecipes.com's content -- only that this environment's requests, using those agents' declared user-agent strings, did not. The robots.txt-level finding stands on its own regardless of this ambiguity, since it is read directly from a plain-text file served without any challenge.

not_assessed.check: Recipe/AggregateRating/Review structured-data completeness on individual recipe pages -- the specific mechanism this site was selected to test
not_assessed.reason: No recipe page, and no sitemap file listing recipe URLs, was reachable from this run's network environment (see above) -- every fetch attempted was challenged or rejected before any page content could be read.
not_assessed.impact: This audit cannot say whether allrecipes.com's Recipe schema (ratings, cook time, ingredients, nutrition) is complete, valid, or agrees with visible text -- the specific question this run set out to answer could not be completed for this site.
